dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Sandra. Good morning.
Good morning, Sandra. Um, yes. I am calling because I want to get a license for my dog. I think it is here that I do this? I am not sure.
You're in the right place, we do dog licenses here. Is it a new dog or are you renewing one?
New to me. We got him, um, in January. He is a small one, brown, he is maybe two years. From a shelter in Fall River.
Aw, lucky dog. Okay, so for a license the main thing we need is proof that he's current on his rabies vaccine.
Yes, this is what I am confused about. The rabies paper. The shelter gave me a, a big folder with many papers. I do not know which one is the one you want.

That's very common. What you're looking for is a rabies certificate. It's usually a single page, it comes from the vet who gave the shot, and it has the dog's name, the date of the vaccine, and when it expires. There's usually a vet's signature or stamp on it.
A stamp. Okay. There is one paper that says, um, vaccination record, with many little lines. Vaccines for the cough, for the distemper, and also rabies. Is this the one?
It could be, if rabies is listed with a date and it's signed by the vet or the clinic. Does it say the date he got it?
Let me look. I have the folder here by the phone. [pause] Yes. It says rabies, and a date in December. And a name of the doctor, but I cannot read it, the handwriting is very bad.
That's all right, we don't need to read the handwriting as long as it's from a clinic and it's clear it's the rabies shot. If it's got a clinic name on top, that usually does it.
There is a clinic name on the top, yes. In Fall River. So this counts? Even if it is from the shelter and not my own doctor?
Usually, yes, if the shelter's vet signed off on it. The vaccine is what matters, not who you are to the vet.
Okay, okay. And a picture of it on my phone, is that good? Or I must have the paper?
I'd bring the actual paper to be safe. You can keep your folder, we'll just look at it and copy it.

Good. So what else do I bring? When I come in person. I want to not come twice, you understand. I am driving a rental car now, my own car is in the shop, so it is not easy for me to go back and forth.

Oh, no, that's a pain. Okay, let's get it right the first time. Bring the rabies certificate, a photo ID, and something that shows your address. Also if he's been spayed or neutered, bring that paperwork, because it can change the fee.
Address. I rent my apartment. I do not own. I have a lease, and I have the electric bill. Which one?
Either one is fine. The bill is easier to carry, honestly. As long as it has your name and the Bellevue address.
Yes, it is 176 Bellevue Avenue. My name on the bill is Holly Peckham. P-E-C-K-H-A-M.
Got it, Holly. And his name?
Biscoito. It is Portuguese, like a cookie. Well, the shelter gave him another name, but we changed it.
Biscoito, I love it. Now, for the paperwork, does the certificate list his name as the shelter named him, or as Biscoito?
The other name. Is a problem?
Not a problem. Just tell the person at the counter, and write both names down if you can. They'll sort it out.
Okay. Both names. And the neuter, I think it is on a different paper. The shelter did it. I think the date is on the same page, but maybe not. I will bring all the folder.
That's the best plan. Bring the whole folder and we'll find what we need.
And where do I go? In City Hall, which door? I was never inside before.

Come into City Hall on Broadway and ask for the City Clerk's office, we're on the main floor. We're open weekdays during regular business hours, so you've got plenty of time today if you want to come this afternoon.
Today, maybe. I must see if I can get the car. Because it is a rental, I have it only until, um, Wednesday. Then I get mine back, I hope.
Well, either way you'll be set. Just take the folder, your ID, and the bill.
ID, bill, folder. And the rabies paper is the one with the vaccine and the date and the stamp. Yes? I say it again so I do not forget.
You've got it exactly. One page, the vaccine, the date, the clinic. If it turns out the page is missing the expiration, the clinic can fill that in, but don't worry about it before you come.
Expiration. Hmm. I did not see this word on it. Maybe it says another way. I will look again at home.
Sometimes it says something like valid for one year or three years. Look for that. If you can't find it, bring it anyway.
Okay. Thank you, Sandra, you are very kind. I was nervous to call, because I did not know the rules.
Anytime, Holly. Give Biscoito a scratch from me. See you soon.
I will. Thank you. Have a good day. Bye-bye.
